description: Every public numeric claim Lazaret makes, each backed by a committed evidence artifact under evidence/ and re-checked by pnpm check:claims. The artifacts are regenerated by the live verification run (fixture parity), the loader and compiler (slice and closure), and scripts/gen-evidence.ts (blast benchmark), and each carries the commit, HydraDB image digest, environment, and raw observations behind the number. A drifted claim fails CI.

claims.statement: On the fixture micro-slice the compiled EXPOSES set equals the reference-model closure exactly: 3 members.
claims.evidence: pnpm verify writes evidence/parity-fixture.json from a live compile-and-compare run.
claims.limitations: Deterministic fixture, checked on every verify run against a live node.

claims.statement: The fixture parity check reports an exact match between the compiled graph and the independent reference model.
claims.evidence: evidence/parity-fixture.json ok flag, set by compareParity during pnpm verify.

claims.statement: The demonstration npm slice loaded into HydraDB contains 3980 packages.
claims.evidence: crawl then load-dir; count recorded in data/slice/load-report.json and copied with provenance into evidence/slice.json by scripts/gen-evidence.ts.
claims.limitations: A bounded slice seeded from npm-high-impact plus incident packages, not all of npm. Counts move with the crawl budget.

claims.statement: The demonstration npm slice contains 31700 versioned nodes.
claims.limitations: Bounded slice; counts move with the crawl budget.

claims.statement: The demonstration npm slice contains 85780 DEPENDS_ON edges.
claims.limitations: Bounded slice; counts move with the crawl budget.

claims.statement: Compiling the September 2025 chalk/debug incident over the slice materialized a 983-version exposure closure from 16 real compromised targets.
claims.evidence: compile writes data/compile-chalk-debug-2025-09.json; scripts/gen-evidence.ts copies members with provenance into evidence/compile-chalk-debug-2025-09.json.
claims.limitations: Closure size depends on the crawled slice. Malicious version numbers and timestamps were reconstructed from the live npm registry time map.

claims.statement: The chalk/debug exposure closure spans 6 dependency levels, depths 0 through 5.
After compilation, a warm full-frame blast query over the 983-member chalk/debug closure returns well under 150 ms; the recorded run measured a 72 ms median.
claims.evidence: evidence/benchmark-blast.json full.p50Ms over 100 samples, server-side HydraDB query time from /v1/blast.
claims.limitations: Local single-node HydraDB on Apple Silicon. Cold first call is recorded separately in the same artifact. Absolute latency moves with hardware.

claims.statement: The warm full-frame blast query stays under 250 ms at the 95th percentile.
claims.limitations: Local single-node HydraDB on Apple Silicon; absolute latency moves with hardware.

claims.statement: The evidence campaign runs against a deterministic cohort of 50 or more real public package-lock.json files, each pinned to a commit SHA.
claims.evidence: fixtures/campaign/manifest.json lists every repo, commit, path and raw URL; scripts/campaign-run.ts records the cohort size in evidence/campaign-report.json.
claims.limitations: Cohort selected before any verdict was computed, from popular public npm repositories that commit a root lockfile.

claims.statement: Across the cohort, the production API and the independent reference model return the same service-level verdict for every lockfile.
claims.evidence: evidence/campaign-report.json serviceAgreement.rate over the full cohort.

claims.statement: The two independent engines agree on at least 99.9% of individual package classifications across the cohort; the recorded run was 37759 of 37759.
claims.evidence: evidence/campaign-report.json packageAgreement.rate; every disagreement, if any, is listed in the same file.
claims.limitations: Production reads the compiled graph in HydraDB; the reference model recomputes the closure from the original crawled records. Shared use of the semver specification is intentional.

claims.statement: Every sampled exposed member's evidence path terminates at a real compromised advisory target.
claims.evidence: evidence/path-audit.json passRate over 100 sampled members walked through /v1/path.

claims.statement: Replaying the blast radius across 100 timestamps returns a warm median well under 150 ms.
claims.evidence: evidence/replay-latency.json warmP50Ms over 100 replay points, server-side HydraDB query time.
claims.limitations: Local single-node HydraDB on Apple Silicon; the cold first call is recorded separately in the same artifact.
